title: Quantized Commit Credit Splitting & Autoscale Failsafe
creator: Ava Martin
description: Proposal to introduce 'quantized commit credits' — fractional reservation units that let enterprise customers split reserved GPU commitments into small, priced credit buckets (e.g., 15-minute and 1-hour units) and pair that with an autoscale failsafe that provides deterministic burst and graceful preemption semantics. The goal is to increase enterprise conversion by lowering lock-in friction while preserving predictable capacity economics and clear SLA boundaries.
background: Sales and AE teams report a common barrier: customers hesitate to sign large GPU commits because their workload patterns are spiky and seasonally bursty. Existing burst features and flexible credits are either too coarse or expose us to unpredictable overage risk. Legal asks for clear contract terms around preemption and reconciliation. Engineering has a prototype for smaller time-sliced reservations but needs pricing and billing semantics defined.
goals: Create a quantified pricing model for fractional commit credits (15min, 1h, 6h bands)
Design contract language and reconciliation flow for burst consumption and preemption windows
Define autoscale failsafe rules that preserve latency SLOs and limit Redwood exposure to overage cost
Pilot with 2 mid-market customers and measure conversion uplift and usage patterns
success_metrics: Pilot conversion rate (signed pilots / engaged leads) >= 20%
Average committed utilization improves by 18% (less unused reserved time)
Revenue at-risk from unexpected burst overruns < $2000/month during pilot
acceptance_criteria: Pricing schedule published in pricing playbook (internal) and GA proposal
Contract addendum drafted and reviewed by legal for preemption, reconciliation and SLA waterfall
Billing system supports fractional credit consumption with 15-minute granularity and provides per-credit audit logs
Runtime supports autoscale failsafe policy with tiered fallback to public-hosted capacity and explicit cost delta reporting
tasks: PM: finalize pricing bands and modeled P&L for 3 scenarios (conservative/target/aggressive)
Legal: draft contract addendum and reconciliation clause for fractional credits
Eng: implement metering prototype and audit logs for fractional credits (ENG-1842)
Eng: autoscale failsafe implementation plan and perf target doc
Design: UX for commit-splitting UI in Console and warning states
Sales: prepare pilot collateral and SOW template
Finance: validate billing reconciliation runbook and dispute flow
notes: Early engineering prototype uses 1-minute tick metering but billing will be rounded to 15-minute buckets
Legal prefers explicit preemption notice windows (e.g., 10 minutes for best-effort burst reclaim)
Consider offering a discounted rate for 6-month pre-buy of quantized credits to encourage conversion
risks: Over-complex billing confusion for customers leading to more support tickets
Edge-case preemption causing transient latency spikes for real-time customers
Potential revenue leakage if reconciliation rules are too lenient
next_steps: Sync with Eng infra to scope meter changes (week of 2025-02-17)
Select 2 pilot customers and finalize SOW by 2025-02-28
